beats.trigger: ## Lecture: Grounded, and four candidates to measure
beats.got: Nothing new; it's a section header.

beats.trigger: Grounded means traceable to a specific file, number or quote in a source.
beats.got: Grounded means I can trace it to a source. That works like an audit trail.

beats.trigger: at 85% each come to about 20% end-to-end: one task in five correct, four in five with a defect
beats.got: Small error rates multiply across steps. I checked it: 0.85 to the tenth is about 0.2. It is the first figure I could verify.

beats.trigger: Say the detector catches 90% of them.
beats.got: Repeated test-and-fix rounds drive errors down fast. The 90% catch rate is assumed, not shown.

beats.trigger: Fluency is not evidence, and the model cannot tell you which parts of its output are grounded.
beats.got: Asking the AI whether it's sure proves nothing. I need an independent check.

beats.trigger: Run several candidate methods in parallel and measure which one catches what your benchmark says it should.
beats.got: Test the methods on my own material before choosing one. I'd do that with any vendor.

beats.trigger: Catches *citation cargo-cult*.
beats.got: Four checks, each catching a different kind of error. The labels are jargon, but the idea is clear enough.

beats.got: The check comes with a written statement of what it misses. That is the risk named before I ask for it.

take_homes: Errors multiply: ten steps at 85% each leaves about one task in five correct, so a long AI workflow needs a check built in.
Asking the AI 'are you sure?' proves nothing. Test the checks on my own material and keep the one with a score.
A good check states what it misses. I'd want that in any control I sign off.

monday.move: Ask my controller to run the month-end variance commentary through an agent once, then check each number in it against the ledger by hand.

monday.stop_condition: Any figure in the commentary that can't be traced to the ledger, or no time saved after the manual check

misconception.why: The module showed that the value sits in a check we build and measure on our own material, not in the tool we license. I still think of it mostly as a licence, since nobody gave a cost or payback.

one_line: The ten-step maths and the scoreboard are useful because I can check them. But a day on a US legal case with no cost or payback figure is a hard sell to the board.
